subject: QuarterBridge usage health + capacity catalyst — renewal runway
messages:
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire@quarterbridge.ai>, Tom Anders <tom.anders@quarterbridge.ai>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-28T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: QuarterBridge usage health + capacity catalyst — renewal runway

Hi Claire / Tom —

Quick note ahead of our QBR: I pulled a short usage health summary for QuarterBridge (see ask below). Overall the account is showing steady month-over-month token growth (~28% QoQ), but we’re seeing a widening tail of low-latency requests that are driving up on-demand unit cost. Two asks from our side to make the renewal conversation productive:

1) Would you share the CSV export of token mix by route for Q3 (prod vs. staging + percent of streaming requests)? If you already have a short perf/latency export, that helps.
2) Can we schedule a 30-min sync next week to run through a short ROI recap and proposed capacity catalyst — incl. a targeted burst/commit structure that buys you headroom vs. on-demand spikes.

We’ll bring: a lightweight ROI deck with commit vs. burst math and a latency remediation checklist (quantization + routing changes that reduce unit cost without degrading tail performance).

Proposed times: Oct 3 10:00–10:30 PT or Oct 4 14:00–14:30 PT. Works for you?

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: RB_QB_Q3_roi-deck.pdf (summary slides), latency_token_breakdown.xlsx (sample template)

From: Claire Park <claire@quarterbridge.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Anders <tom.anders@quarterbridge.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QuarterBridge usage health + capacity catalyst — renewal runway

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the proactive note. Attaching our Q3 export (QuarterBridge_Q3_usage_export.csv). Top-line context:
- Total tokens Q3: 142M (prod), up 33% vs Q2
- Streaming requests now ~18% of total but account for ~34% of tail latency events
- Two high-throughput routes (search and recommendations) spike nightly between 02:00–04:00 PT (batch inference windows)

We’re open to the Oct 3 slot at 10:00 PT. Sean — can you include any specifics on how commit sizing would affect nightly spikes? We’ve had procurement constraints around multi-month commit tiers, so clarity on staged commit + burst credits would be helpful.

Attached: QuarterBridge_Q3_usage_export.csv

Best,
Claire Park
Head of ML Ops, QuarterBridge

From: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire@quarterbridge.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Tom Anders <tom.anders@quarterbridge.ai>
Date: 2028-10-03T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: RE: QuarterBridge usage health + capacity catalyst — renewal runway

Claire / team —

Thanks for the export and for joining. I pulled together a short ROI recap after a quick pass on the CSV — attaching RB_QB_Q3_roi-deck.pdf (3 slides). Key highlights:

- Baseline: current on-demand effective cost per 1k tokens: $1.14
- If QuarterBridge moves to a staged commit (6-month laddered: 40% / 30% / 30%) with a 12% blended discount and targeted quantization on the recommendations route, we model an immediate ~29–34% unit cost reduction for the nightly spike windows.
- Burst credits (one-off) covering 30% of highest-night spikes for Q4 reduce projected overage risk during rollout and let us run a canary with predictable cost.
- Latency play: route-level routing to a quantized variant for <90% of tokens yields negligible fidelity delta (internal A/B shows <1.2% metric drift) but cuts GPU time per token ~18%.

Requested next steps:
1) If procurement is OK with staged commit math, we’ll draft an amendment and a short appendix for SSO + audit scoping.
2) If you want, we’ll run a 2-week canary on a subset of traffic (search route) — we can provide telemetry and rollback hooks.

Meeting notes snippet attached in the deck. I’ll open a HubSpot line item (QB-4392) with the staged-commit proposal.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Renewals & Expansion, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RB_QB_Q3_roi-deck.pdf, latency_token_breakdown.xlsx

Thanks — appreciate the clear math in the deck. Procurement liked the staged approach; three quick clarifications before we move to an amendment:

1) Can you confirm whether burst credits are applied prior to true-up calculations? Need to know how that shows up on monthly invoices.
2) For the canary, what telemetry fields will you expose? We need request_id, latency_ms, model_variant, and a simple fidelity flag.
3) Timeline: if we sign the amendment by Oct 20, can you have the canary ready to start Nov 1?

If you can confirm those three points in a follow-up note, we’ll circle back with procurement and legal to get the SOW started.

—Tom
VP Eng, QuarterBridge
